This app runs a recompiled Xbox game on Android. The game itself is not included: you bring your own copy, from a disc you own. Setting it up takes a minute, or a few for a disc image.
The folder of your extracted disc, or a disc image (.iso)
The app checks it is the right game, and copies or extracts it if needed
Settings and game data stay one press away
Use a game you own: the folder of your extracted disc, or a disc image you made yourself. Your current game stays until the new one has been checked.
The extracted disc: default.xbe and its files, on the device or an SD card. Read in place with All files access, otherwise copied into the app.
A .iso or .xiso image of your disc. Extracted once into the app\'s storage: it needs the game\'s size free and takes a few minutes.

With « All files access », the app reads the game straight from the folder you choose, on the phone or on an SD card: no copy, and it works for a 4 GB disc. The app only reads the game folder you pick.\n\nWithout it, the folder is copied into the app\'s own storage: that takes as much free space again and a few minutes, and the copy is removed with the app.
Opens the system page: turn it on for this app, come back, then pick the folder.
No permission. The folder is copied into the app\'s storage: as much free space again, a few minutes; removed with the app.
Your current game is kept until the new one has been checked. Keep the app open until the end.
The game is already running: Play brings it back where you left it.
Saved in %1$s and applied the next time the game starts. Lines you add there yourself are kept.
Next time, the game opens directly. Long-press the app icon › Launcher to come back here.
Next time, this screen shows first.

The language the Xbox tells the game. The game shows its menus, text and voices in it when its disc has that language (a European disc usually does, a US disc is often English only); otherwise the game picks one itself, usually English. « Same as Android » follows the phone\'s language. A game can have its own in the in-game menu (Quick settings). Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_LANGUAGE)
On: the app icon starts the game straight away when it is set up. Off: this screen shows first, with Play selected.
Saved. Applied the next time the game starts.
Saved. The game is running: it uses the new setting after it is restarted.
The game is running: changes apply the next time it starts.
Puts every option on this screen back to its default, by removing its lines from recomp.cfg. Other lines in the file are left as they are.
Defaults restored. Applied the next time the game starts.
On: frames are shown in step with the display, without tearing. Off: frames are shown as soon as they are ready; a little less delay, but the picture can tear. (RECOMP_PRESENT_VSYNC)

GPU: the game is drawn with OpenGL ES, many times faster than software. Software: drawn by the CPU, slower, for comparing or when a game shows something wrong on the GPU. Auto: GPU, unless this game\'s profile asks for software. If the GPU cannot start (no OpenGL ES 3.0), the game falls back to software on its own. (RECOMP_GPU)

With the GPU renderer, menus and pause screens can run at 200 frames per second or more, which only drains the battery and heats the device. The cap holds them to 60 (or 30). Auto: the game\'s own rate (60, or 30 when it asks for 30), or a steady lower rate (30) when the device cannot keep it up; a game whose logic follows the frame rate is never slowed down. 30 or 60: a fixed cap, with the GPU renderer only. Off removes it, for testing. (RECOMP_GPU_FPS_CAP; Auto is RECOMP_PACING=auto)

The GPU renderer can draw the 3D picture at 2 or 3 times the console\'s resolution, or at the size that fits the screen exactly. Sharper, at the cost of more GPU work, heat and battery. Effects such as bloom and shadows keep their original resolution. Auto: what this game\'s profile chooses (1× for now). No effect with the software renderer. (RECOMP_GPU_SCALE)

Tells the game the TV is 16:9, as the Xbox dashboard setting did. A game that supports it then draws a wider picture; set Aspect ratio to 16:9 to show it full width. A game without widescreen support ignores it. Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_WIDESCREEN)

Tells the game the TV takes progressive 480p, as the Xbox dashboard setting did with the HD cable. A game that offers it renders full frames instead of interlaced ones; others ignore it. Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_480P)

Auto shows the game in 16:9 when it can draw a wider picture, and keeps menus and videos in their original shape. 4:3 always shows the console\'s original picture with side bars. 16:9 always fills the screen; a game without widescreen support is stretched.

Sharp takes the nearest texel, as the game is drawn by default. Smooth blends four texels; anisotropic also follows surfaces seen at an angle. Smoother modes cost speed, and are not the default because they change the look the game was tested with. (RECOMP_TEX_BILINEAR, RECOMP_TEX_ANISO)
On: sounds the game places in 3D are filtered to sound like they come from their direction, best with headphones. Off: plain stereo panning. (RECOMP_APU_HRTF)

The size of each buffer handed to the device, in samples (256, 512, 1024, 2048). Short: less delay between the picture and the sound. Long: fewer crackles and drop-outs on a busy device. (RECOMP_AUDIO_BUF_SAMPLES)

Threads of the software renderer that share large triangles and vertex shading. Auto uses every core the game runs on but one (the fast cores when "Fast cores" is on). More can be faster on a big SoC; fewer can help when the game itself is short of cores. (RECOMP_RASTER_THREADS)
On: the game runs on the SoC\'s fast cores only, as set at start. Off: the system may also put it on the slow cores; try it only if the game stutters with this on. (RECOMP_BIG_CORES)

Runs the runtime\'s self-test before the game starts and writes one PASS or FAIL line per check to the log (logcat, tag xboxrecomp). Useful in a bug report; the game then starts as usual. (RECOMP_SHELL_SELFTEST)
Pick a game folder or a disc image. The current game stays until the new one has been checked; a running game is closed then. Saves are kept.
Removes %1$s, the copy this app made. Your saves stay (internal storage). You then choose the game again to play.
Press A again within 5 seconds to delete the imported copy.
The imported copy was deleted. Saves are kept.
A statically recompiled game, run by XRecomp (the xboxrecomp runtime) on Android arm64. No game data is included: the app reads the copy you set up from a disc you own.
XRecomp and xboxrecomp: MIT. SDL2: zlib. CPython: PSF. LLVM: Apache 2.0 with LLVM exceptions. Capstone: BSD.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by the console\'s or the game\'s makers. Use only games you own.
The licence texts are missing from this build: see NOTICE and LICENSES/ in the source repository.
A shortcut on your home screen with this game\'s logo. Tapping it opens this game: it starts when it is ready, otherwise its page shows what it needs.
Shortcut requested: confirm it in your home screen\'s dialog.
Your home screen did not accept the shortcut.
The game of this shortcut is no longer in the library: choose one here.

Makes this game an app of its own on this device: its name and logo in your apps, locked to this disc, opening straight into it. It is a copy of XRecomp, so it takes about %1$s. Android asks you to confirm the install. For your own use only.
Prepare this game first (Home › Prepare): its own app is made from the prepared game, so that it starts straight into it.
Prepare %1$s first, then Create an app.
Allow XRecomp to install apps on the screen that opened, then come back and press Create an app again.
%1$s is ready: confirm the install in Android\'s dialog.
%1$s is installed: find it in your apps. Open it and choose this game once; it opens straight into it from then on.
An app %1$s signed by another key is installed: uninstall it, then create the app again.
The app could not be created: %1$s. Nothing was installed.
Not enough internal storage to prepare the game: %1$s needed, %2$s free.
This device has %1$s of memory: preparing may be slow or fail (6 GB or more recommended).
You can leave the app: it carries on in the background.
Press again to cancel the preparation.
The preparation was cancelled. What was done is kept: Resume carries on from there.
The game crashed, and this run found code the last preparation missed. Prepare again takes it in, then starts the game.
The game crashed and preparing again cannot help: %1$s.
The last run met code the preparation had missed: the game is prepared again with it, in the background. You can play meanwhile; the next start uses the new version. Stop ends it.
The last run met code the preparation had missed (%1$d). Prepare again takes it in, in the background; Play stays.
The game crashed on code the preparation had missed: preparing it again with it (round %1$d), then the game starts by itself. B stops it; Settings › General › Self-healing turns this off.
Stopped. The game keeps its current preparation.
The preparation was interrupted (the system closed it). What was done is kept: Prepare carries on from there.
The system stopped the compiler twice (not enough memory, or Android\'s limit on background processes). Close other apps and retry.
Internal storage is full (%1$s free). Free some space, then retry: what was done is kept.
No app on this device can receive the log.
Progress of the game\'s preparation, with Cancel
Ready: open the app and press Play.
The preparation failed (%1$s). Open the app to see why.
In the game, Back opens the game menu (settings, quit). Saves stay on this device.
Made once, here on the device, from your own copy: then Play starts at once.
Preparing your game. You can leave the app: it carries on in the background.
The preparation stopped on an error. See why, then retry from where it stopped.

On: a soft tick when the selection moves or a value changes, and short sounds to select, go back, for an error and when the game is ready. Off: the launcher is silent. The game\'s own sound is not affected.
On: the device gives a light buzz when the selection moves, a press, an error and when the game is ready. Android\'s own « touch feedback » setting must be on too. Off: no buzz from the launcher.
On: when a run meets code the preparation missed, the app prepares the game again by itself (after a crash, then starts it again), with a note you can act on. Off: it offers Prepare again instead.
Self-healing off: Prepare again is offered instead.

Panel: the game\'s card and buttons here, and in the game the Xbox buttons the device lacks (Black, White, Back, Start) and a few tools. Black: the second screen stays black. Off: the app leaves it to the system.
The same for any gamepad Android sees: the game reads it as the first Xbox controller. Buttons are taken by position, as Android names them.

Lossless Scaling frame generation (LSFG 3.1) draws one frame between every two the game renders: the game runs at 30 frames per second and the screen shows 60. It needs your own copy of Lossless.dll (Choose Lossless.dll below) and Vulkan. Moving text and the HUD can wobble, a scene cut can ghost for one frame, and input waits one frame longer. 2× performance uses the lighter shader set, for when 2× is too heavy for the device. If generation fails or is too slow, the game goes back to normal frames on its own. Xbox: needs the GPU renderer for the 30 fps pacing. GBA, PS1, N64: the game keeps its own speed; the frames it shows twice or three times are replaced by drawn ones, a game that already shows 60 is left as it is; a game can have its own setting in its Options. (RECOMP_LSFG, RECOMP_LSFG_MULT, RECOMP_LSFG_PERF)

Frame generation uses the shaders of Lossless Scaling, which you must own (Steam). Copy Lossless.dll from your Lossless Scaling folder (steamapps/common/Lossless Scaling) to this device and choose it here. Only its shaders are kept, in the app\'s private storage; the DLL itself is read once and never stored.
Lossless.dll is never included in the app or shared; the shaders stay on this device.
This Lossless.dll version is not supported
Frame generation unavailable for this title

This game\'s pack turns frame generation off (pack.json env_force RECOMP_LSFG=0). The setting stays for your other games. (Without such a setting, frame generation decides by itself: it waits 25 to 50 seconds after the game starts and stays off for a game locked to 60 frames per second, whose logic would run in slow motion at frame generation\'s 30.)
Shaders found, but this app cannot translate them (translator missing)
%1$s is not a DLL: choose Lossless.dll.

The launcher takes its colours, and a faint backdrop, from the title image of %1$s, read from your copy of the game. The status colours (ready, warnings, errors) stay the same. Colours only: no backdrop image. Off: the launcher\'s own green.

The Vulkan driver games use by default (for now only the Nintendo 64 Vulkan renderer uses one): the device\'s own, or a Mesa Turnip driver you download or import. A game can have its own in its Options. If the chosen driver does not work, the game falls back to the device\'s driver, then to the software renderer.
This app uses the Vulkan driver chosen in XRecomp (Nintendo 64 Vulkan renderer only, for now), taken again at each start. Change it in XRecomp.
The driver is chosen in XRecomp; this app follows it at its next start.
The device\'s own Vulkan driver (Qualcomm\'s on a Snapdragon). Always there.
This driver crashed the game at its last start: it is skipped (system driver) until you choose it again.
At its last start this driver could not be opened, or the renderer could not run on it: the system driver was used.
At its last start this driver was not loaded (Android kept the device\'s own driver): the system driver was used.
Not compatible with the N64 renderer: at its last start this driver loaded, but the Nintendo 64 Vulkan renderer (paraLLEl-RDP) cannot run on it. The system driver was used.
At its last start this driver could not be opened: the system driver was used.

The Vulkan driver this game\'s Nintendo 64 Vulkan renderer uses: as in Settings › Graphics › Vulkan driver, the device\'s own (System), or one of the installed drivers. Applies the next time the game starts.
A: make it the default for every game (a game can have its own in its Options). X twice: delete it (games that chose it go back to the default).
A pre-release: its author marks it as not final.
A: download and install it. Its size and checksum are checked against GitHub\'s listing.
No list yet. Refresh to look for drivers.
Asks GitHub for the latest releases of MrPurple666/purple-turnip and K11MCH1/AdrenoToolsDrivers (Turnip builds only). The only time XRecomp uses the network.
An adrenotools driver package (a .zip with meta.json and the driver library) from this device\'s storage.
Drivers come from third parties, are never part of the app, and run as native code inside it.

X deletes an installed driver: move to one first.
Vulkan driver: %1$s. The game running now keeps its driver until it is started again.
The choice could not be saved.
A game is running: a new choice applies at its next start.
%1$s installed. Press A to use it.
This file is not a zip. Nothing was kept.

This package is too large (over 256 MB). Nothing was kept.
The driver library is not a 64-bit ARM library. Nothing was kept.
This driver needs a newer version of Android. Nothing was kept.

On: the box art of your GBA, PlayStation and N64 games comes from libretro-thumbnails (the game\'s file name is looked up on GitHub). Off: nothing is downloaded; a picture of the game is kept once you have played it.
Covers are looked for at the next library scan.
